sections.h2: Choosing how to sell in Brentwood
sections.html:
Brentwood is a Williamson County suburb south of Nashville. Roughly nine in ten homes (90.4 percent) are owner occupied, with a typical value of $1,031,300. Population was estimated at 45,313 on July 1, 2025, 0.1 percent below April 2020. Most sales now involve existing houses rather than new lots, and with values this high every route involves large sums.

Your choices are a listing, a do-it-yourself sale or a cash buyer who takes the house as it is. Weigh how long the house needs and how much carrying cost you can absorb. Cash suits a house with deferred repairs, an estate on a deadline, or a family that cannot keep the place show-ready. A listing makes sense when the house is in good shape and can wait a few months.

The gap between $3,406 and $895 a month shows how much equity many owners hold. If your house is paid off, even a discounted quick sale can leave real cash after closing.

Tornadoes have touched Brentwood on December 24, 1988, January 30, 2013 and March 1, 2017, so buyers ask about the roof first. Inspectors in Brentwood keep returning to the same items:

  • Roof age and storm damage history.
  • Drainage around the foundation.
  • Heating and cooling systems.

None of these is unusual, but each can delay a conventional closing if the buyer's lender wants repairs done first. A cash buyer builds the repair cost into the offer, so there is nothing to haggle over afterward.

sections.h2: Brentwood tax bills and due dates
sections.html:
The Williamson County Trustee bills and collects Brentwood city taxes. One combined city and county notice goes out in early October. Payment is penalty-free from October 1 to the last day of February (February 28). Starting March 1, interest of 1.5 percent per month accrues. The payment office is at 1320 W Main St, Suite 203, Franklin, and the Trustee line is 615-790-5709.

The 2026 county rate table puts Brentwood at 19 cents city plus $1.30 county, a combined $1.49 on each $100 of assessed value. Assessed value is 25 percent of appraised value.

The January 1 owner is the one who gets the notice. Sell in the fall and the bill still arrives under your name, so the closing statement must split the year with the buyer. Ask the title company to figure that split and compare it with the Trustee's record.

Your first call goes to the county Assessor of Property at 615-790-5708. If that does not settle it, the equalization board hears appeals in June, and you book a slot by phoning the assessor in the first days of that month. Only the owner on the roll or an authorized agent may file. Five residents serve on the board, appointed by the County Commission for two-year terms.

A call can fix a simple mistake like wrong square footage, but it is no substitute for the board hearing. If you skip that hearing, the appeal can end there, since a disputed assessment generally has to be heard locally first.

If you go on to the state, file by August 1 of the tax year or 45 days after the local notice, whichever is later. Bring recent sales of similar houses, adjusted for size, age, condition and location. A professional appraisal also works.

sections.h2: Can I rent my Brentwood house short term before it sells?
sections.html:
Generally no, if the house sits in a single-family district. Municipal code Section 78-19(e) bars stays under three months in those districts, and the city has cited owners who kept renting after a warning.

Counting on Airbnb income to cover carrying costs during the listing period will not work here. A lease of three months or longer is a different matter, but confirm with Planning and Codes at 615-371-2204 before advertising. Buyers and their lenders also tend to read recent citations as a red flag.

Building work follows a separate path. The Codes Section accepts permit applications electronically and takes fee checks at 5211 Maryland Way. Clear up open or expired permits before listing, since they surface in a buyer's inspection.

sections.h2: Recording the deed and state taxes
sections.html:
The recording office is in Franklin: Williamson County Register of Deeds, 1320 West Main Street, Suite 201, 615-790-5706, open 8:00 am to 4:30 pm on weekdays. Tennessee's realty transfer tax comes to 37 cents on every $100 of price. Debt secured by a recorded deed of trust also carries a mortgage tax of $0.115 per $100, and the first $2,000 is exempt. Your title company runs the numbers and files the deed. A cash deal has no lender checklist, so the paperwork is lighter, but the deed is recorded the same way.

  • Bring a payoff statement from any lender holding a lien.
  • Confirm every owner on the deed will sign before a notary.
  • Request a tax proration based on the Trustee's own record.

sections.h2: Ways to sell fast in Brentwood
sections.html:
Three tracks are workable here, and each trades price against speed differently.

  • An as-is cash purchase: the buyer inspects, makes an offer, and closes on the date you pick. You skip repairs, showings and lender conditions.
  • A pre-listing renovation: you fix the roof, drainage and mechanical items, then list at full market value. This returns more money but takes months and cash up front.
  • A private sale to a neighbor or relative, which works if both sides have financing ready and agree on price.

From any buyer, get proof of funds, a written closing date and the name of the title company. Compare the net figure after taxes, payoff and recording, not the headline number.

Before accepting, collect your payoff letter, your latest tax notice and a list of everyone named on the deed. Cash sales usually involve less back and forth since no underwriter is involved. Occupied or inherited houses still need title review time, so say up front if an estate or several owners are involved.

faqs.q: How fast can a Brentwood house sell for cash?
faqs.a: The timeline depends on payoff letters, any estate paperwork and how fast the Williamson County Register of Deeds can record the deed. Occupied or inherited houses usually need extra days for title review.

faqs.q: Do I still owe property tax after selling a Brentwood house?
faqs.a: Yes, for the part of the year you held it, and the closing statement normally divides the bill. The county notice is sent to the January 1 titleholder. Call the Trustee at 615-790-5709 to check whether this year is paid.

faqs.q: What is the Brentwood city property tax rate?
faqs.a: The 2026 county table shows 19 cents per $100 of assessed value for the city, plus $1.30 for the county, or $1.49 combined. Assessment is 25 percent of appraisal. Your own bill may differ if a relief program applies, so ask the Trustee.

faqs.q: Can I put my Brentwood home on a short-term rental site while I wait to sell?
faqs.a: Not in a single-family district for stays under three months, because Section 78-19(e) of the city code prohibits it. Call Planning and Codes at 615-371-2204 before renting.

faqs.q: Which office records a Brentwood deed?
faqs.a: Brentwood City Hall does not record deeds. Take them to the Register of Deeds in Franklin (1320 West Main Street, Suite 201, 615-790-5706), where the 37 cents per $100 state transfer tax is collected.
